name: Evidence-licensed dialogue
principle: Every answer must be licensed by evidence already in the store. If no warrant exists, the only permitted answer is Unknown. An answer that cannot be recomputed from the store is a contract violation, not a mistake.
rationale: Without this rule 'conversational reasoning' cannot be checked: fluent text can always be produced, so nothing distinguishes knowing from sounding like knowing. Licensing every answer makes the boundary between the two mechanical.

answerStates.Answered: A warranted answer drawn from the declared answer schema.
answerStates.Unknown: No warrant exists. MUST carry the reason and what is missing.
answerStates.Refused: The question type is outside the declared scope. Never guessed.
answerStates.Inconsistent: The store itself is contradictory, so no answer is licensed. STORE-WIDE: nothing is answerable.
answerStates.Contested: Warranted evidence exists but disagrees with itself. MUST name both sides and what they disagree about. LOCAL: it concerns one claim and must never block another question — that distinction is the whole reason it is separate from Inconsistent.

invariants.rule: Answered implies warrant.refs is non-empty, or warrant.kind is 'store', or warrant.noEvidence is true — the last case being an explicitly declared derivation over an EMPTY evidence set (a Q4 counterfactual that withdrew a construction's last record). An empty refs is never silent: the flag must be set.
invariants.note: Added when the minimal falsifiable set landed: with 2 labels per construction, withdrawing the LAST one reduces the derivation's evidence set to empty, and I1 as originally written made that case unrepresentable — so 'the last evidence was withdrawn' could not be reported at all. Found by strengthening the I6 test.

invariants.rule: Unknown implies both reason and missing are present.
No free-text answer field exists. Every Answered payload conforms to the question type's declared answer schema.
A question whose type is not declared here is Refused, never answered by analogy.
Every Answered answer must be reproducible from the store alone; the recomputation must agree with what was returned.
Answers are never cached as truth. Adding or removing evidence may change an earlier answer, including turning Answered back into Unknown.
Contested requires at least two disagreeing records and MUST name them, with each side's judge and basis. It may never be returned as a bare state.

Contested is LOCAL and Inconsistent takes precedence: a store-wide failure licenses nothing, so Contested must not be used to report one. Conversely, a contested claim must not prevent any other claim or question from being answered.

questionTypes.name: reading
questionTypes.ask: In this sentence, which entity is the agent, which the recipient, which the theme?
requires: text parses under a declared grammar version
that construction's role mapping is determined: replay(evidence) leaves exactly 1 of 6 permutations
questionTypes.answer: { roles: {agent, recipient, theme}, construction, grammar, occurrences[] }
questionTypes.warrant: evidence — the record ids whose labels pinned the surviving mapping
questionTypes.verify: re-run replay(evidence); the answer must equal candidates[0]

questionTypes.name: comparison
questionTypes.ask: Do these two sentences express the same relation, a role reversal, or different relations?
requires: Q1 is Answered for both a and b
questionTypes.warrant: evidence — the union of both readings' warrants
questionTypes.verify: recompute both readings and re-derive the relation
questionTypes.failClosed: either side Unknown -> Unknown carrying that side's reason

questionTypes.name: warrant
questionTypes.ask: What licenses this conclusion, and who asserted it?
requires: nothing beyond the store: this is the 'how do you know?' move
questionTypes.answer: { refs: [{ id, text, expected, labelKind, labelBy, source }] }
questionTypes.warrant: store — the records named by the answer
questionTypes.verify: each ref must exist in the store and its contentHash must verify
questionTypes.failClosed: an Answered answer with no refs cannot exist (see I1)

questionTypes.name: counterfactual
questionTypes.ask: If evidence record E were withdrawn, would this conclusion still hold?
requires: the named record exists in the store
questionTypes.failClosed: removal that empties a construction -> Answered with survivingRoleMappings 6 and changed true, i.e. the conclusion is retracted

questionTypes.name: consistency
questionTypes.warrant: store — content hashes plus replay over the whole store
questionTypes.failClosed: contradictory evidence -> Inconsistent, and no other question type may return Answered

questionTypes.name: judgement
questionTypes.ask: What have recorded judgements concluded about this claim?
questionTypes.input: { claim: { type, text, ...type-specific fields } } — claim types are declared in tools/semantics/contract.json
requires: the claim type is declared in wenyan.semantics.contract.v1 and is not declared out of scope
at least one judgement recorded about that claim
questionTypes.answer: { verdict: 'holds' | 'fails', judges: n, claimHash } or { disagreement: { holds[], fails[] } }
questionTypes.warrant: judgement — the ids of every judgement recorded about this claim
questionTypes.verify: reload the judgement store; recompute the claim hash; recompute agreement — no cached verdict is trusted
questionTypes.failClosed: no judgement -> Unknown(no-judgement-recorded); undeclared or out-of-scope claim type -> Refused
questionTypes.note: This is the only question type whose warrant is a judgement rather than a text span. Disagreement yields Contested with both sides named; no majority is taken.

questionTypes.name: gloss
questionTypes.reason: Answering would require a lexicon, sense inventory or translation model. None exists in this repository, and no amount of relation evidence creates one.
questionTypes.behaviour: Refused, with this reason. Declared explicitly so its absence stays visible instead of being papered over with fluent text.
questionTypes.wouldRequire: a separate contract for lexical semantics, its own evidence format and its own falsification procedure

notDeclared: Any question type not listed above is Refused (I4). Adding a type means editing this contract first, not extending a prompt.
nonclaims: not a chatbot: there is no natural-language understanding anywhere in this path
not generation: the system never composes prose; every answer is a structured value or Unknown/Refused
not open-domain: the declared question types are the whole of what can be asked
no claim that a warranted answer about a controlled construction says anything about a real text
Q6 gloss is out of scope by declaration, not by temporary limitation
